Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing: H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs — next steps

Hi Tim — great chat last week. Per our call I put together a couple of immediate options so you and procurement can start sizing the committed pool. I attached the inference profile you shared, and a quick capacity workbook.

Quick recap of the things we need to decide (short checklist):
- Latency SLO target (p95) — you mentioned 200 ms as an initial goal
- Long-sequence exposure — percentage of requests > 2k tokens
- Peak RPS and desired burst cushion
- Commit/billing cadence (monthly vs annual)

Two recommended approaches (high-level):
1) Latency-first (workloads with long sequences): H100-heavy cluster for sustained long-seq perf and larger KV cache residency. Example starting point: 2x H100 nodes for warm KV-critical lanes + A100s for baseline throughput.
2) Cost-first (shorter inputs, high TPS): L4 primary fleet for inexpensive per-token, with a small A100 pool to absorb rare long sequences and to host unquantized variants.

Tradeoffs to highlight:
- H100: best raw TFLOPS/FP16 for long sequences and large context, higher hourly cost, good when >5% of requests are long or when you need tight 100–200 ms p95 on 2k+ tokens.
- A100: balanced memory & throughput, cheaper than H100 for medium sequences, better at hosting 70B unquantized models with full precision KV cache.
- L4: lowest cost per token for short-context (<=512) workloads, quantization-friendly. Not great if you need large KV cache or lots of long-context hot paths.

Next steps I propose: if you can confirm the p95 and peak RPS, we’ll finalize a 30-day pilot configuration and show expected reserved commit + burst plan (rows in capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx).

Attachments: stratus_infer_profile.csv (CSV), capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks — happy to walk through the workbook in a quick call.

—

Laura / Dev — feeding Tim’s numbers into the workbook. Summary of the reasoning and recommended pilot fleet below (for the 90-day pilot):

Workload summary from Tim: avg seq 512, 5% > 2048, peak 28 RPS, p95 target 200 ms. Region: us-west.

Operational constraints we should encode:
- Reserve a small H100 pool for long-seq hot paths + fast p95. One H100 can serve ~4 simultaneous long 2k-token requests at ~180–220 ms p95 depending on batching; numbers will vary by quantization.
- A100s are our middle ground: good for hosting FP16 unquantized variant and for moderate sequences. An A100 can sustain ~8 medium (512 token) requests concurrently at p95 ~160–200 ms with batching tuned.
- L4 provides the best token economics for short inputs: for 512-token avg payloads and high TPS, L4 cost/token is ~60–70% lower than H100 in our measurements. However, L4 struggles for context > 2k due to smaller KV cache and memory constraints.

Pilot fleet (90-day):
- 16 x L4 (baseline throughput lane)
- 4 x A100 (service medium-length and host FP16 variant)
- 2 x H100 (warm hot-path for long sequences + headroom)
- Autoscale policy: maintain L4 baseline, scale A100s with queue/backpressure, and failover long requests to H100. Burst buffer: allow +30% ephemeral capacity for 1-hour windows.

Cost & performance notes (estimates):
- Expected reserved commit: ~USD 90k/month equivalent (annualized pricing will reduce unit cost by ~18%).
- Unit economics: L4 cost/token ~0.0008 USD (512 tokens), A100 ~0.0025 USD, H100 ~0.0045 USD — these are pilot estimates and depend on batching and KV cache hitrates.
- Risk: If long-tail exceeds 8% consistently, we should increase H100s and/or shift unquantized traffic to A100 replicas.

Action items:
- Dev: can you validate the per-node concurrency numbers in capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx? I used conservative batch sizes (b=4 for long, b=8 for medium).
- Laura: if this looks OK, I’ll put together a pilot SOW and a pricing slide for procurement.

Attached: capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx, fleet_sketch_hybrid.png

Thanks — I recommend we present this to Tim and procurement as our recommended pilot with a backup plan to expand H100s if their long-tail bumps during the pilot.
